What We Do
  
  
Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight.
  
  
Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.
  
  
We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.
  
  
**Who We Are**
Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.
  
  
The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.
  
  
Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.
  
  
Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software.
  
  
**Who We Need**
As an Applied AI Engineer on Rillet's AI & ML team, you'll design and ship production AI systems that transform how finance and accounting teams operate. This team sits at the intersection of LLMs, ERP workflows, and financial data, building the intelligence layer that makes Rillet fundamentally different from legacy ERP. You'll own high-impact features end-to-end, from model integration to infrastructure, and your work will be used daily by finance teams at companies like Juicebox, Scribe, and Sotheby’s.
  
  
We're an AI-native company, and we expect our engineers to bring that same mindset to how they work. If you're energized by pushing the boundaries of what AI can do in a real product context, you'll fit right in.
  
  
We’re looking for teammates who are based near our New York City or San Francisco offices, or open to relocating. Our hybrid schedule brings the team together in person on Tuesdays and Thursdays, plus one additional flexible day each week. Some roles may spend more time in the office depending on the needs of the team.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Own AI features end-to-end: from designing agentic systems to the infrastructure that runs them in production at scale.
* Work on genuinely hard problems: financial data is structured, high-stakes, and unforgiving, making it one of the more interesting domains to apply LLMs to.
* Build the evaluation frameworks and experimentation loops that turn good models into reliable, production-grade systems.
* Partner directly with product and domain experts to push the frontier of what AI can do inside an ERP, not just what's been done before.

**Who We're Looking For**

* 3+ years in a technical role with a strong foundation in Machine Learning and data analysis or backend systems
* 2+ years shipping production AI systems with real users and real stakes
* Hands-on experience with production LLM applications: agentic systems and offline/online evals to make them reliable
* Proficiency in Python and comfort working across the full stack to deliver end-to-end features
* Strong product instincts and a habit of thinking about user impact, not just technical correctness
* Drawn to hard, ambiguous problems and energized by building in an environment where the playbook is still being written

**Bonus Points**

* Background in fintech, ERP, or accounting software
* Familiarity with Python, Kotlin or TypeScript
* Experience building AI systems that operate on structured financial or transactional data

The expected base salary range for this role is
**$160,000–$350,000**
in New York City and San Francisco. Final compensation within this range will depend on factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and the scope of the role. This role is also eligible for equity and benefits.
  
  
**Note:**
All official Rillet recruiting communications will come from an
**@**
**rillet.com**
email address. If you’re contacted from another domain, please disregard the message and report it as spam.
  
  
**Life at Rillet**

* Grow with us. Take meaningful ownership, expand your scope, and make an impact as Rillet scales.
* Competitive pay and meaningful equity. Be rewarded for the value you help create.
* Benefits that support you. We offer competitive benefits designed to support your health, wellbeing, time away from work, family, and long-term financial goals.
* Better together. We value collaboration, connection, and spending meaningful time together as a team. We regularly create opportunities to connect through team meals, events, and company gatherings.

Two openings on a growing Data Operations team, building an enterprise data platform from the ground up.
 



  





 This is a fully remote role with a U.S.\-based professional services firm. Their technology, AI and data teams are expanding fast, and you’d be joining at exactly the right moment.
 



  





 The team is building its data platform on Microsoft Fabric. The Data Engineers own the core pipelines, and you’ll be the Python engineer who handles everything around them: building custom integrations with third\-party APIs, pulling data out of older systems that don’t connect easily, parsing messy and deeply nested data, and automating routine work alongside the Cloud and Database teams. No two weeks look the same, and you’ll be the person the team turns to when the standard tools can’t solve a problem.
 



  





 This role suits a software engineer who enjoys working with data, rather than a data engineer or data scientist. You’ll have strong production Python experience, ideally from backend, integrations or automation work, and you’ll be comfortable consuming RESTful APIs and dealing with authentication, pagination and rate limits. You’ll parse and transform JSON, XML and CSV using Pandas, write solid SQL, and have some exposure to PySpark or a platform like Fabric, Databricks or Synapse. You write clean, tested code, use Git and CI/CD as standard, and know that a “quick script” often ends up being something the business relies on.
 



  





 Just as important, you can connect your work to the bigger picture. You’ll be working with stakeholders across the firm, so you’ll need to understand what the business needs, explain technical trade\-offs in plain terms, and show how your work makes a difference.
 



  





 You’ll get full remote flexibility, hands\-on experience with a modern data platform, and a real part in the AI and data initiatives shaping how the firm operates.

Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.
Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!
If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.
Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!
About the Role
At Lightmatter, we build photonic interconnect chips designed for large-scale AI compute clusters. As an Embedded Software Engineer for our products. You will develop the control, telemetry, monitoring, and stabilization firmware that maintains the health and lock of our optical transceivers, alongside the tooling required for system bring-up. Collaborating directly with systems, digital, analog, and photonics engineers, you will develop well-defined firmware components through their full lifecycle—from initial requirements to final release—while acquiring deep domain expertise in an emerging field.
Core Responsibilities
Develop the lifecycle (requirements, bring-up, testing, and release) of well-defined optical transceiver firmware modules covering control, telemetry, diagnostics, and monitoring.
Implement and refine photonic control and stabilization loops on embedded targets in partnership with analog and photonics design teams.
Partner with hardware engineers during new board bring-up, utilizing oscilloscopes, logic-analyzers, JTAG, and GDB for debugging.
Participate in control and diagnostics design reviews, documenting findings for cross-functional engineering teams.
Operate independently with guidance at key project milestones.
Qualifications
Experience delivering firmware to production hardware or customers, with clear ownership of specific components.
Proficiency in C or C++ on resource-constrained targets, combined with Python skills for prototyping, test creation, and data analysis.
Solid understanding of embedded communication buses and peripherals (SPI, I2C, GPIO, UART) and hardware–software co-integration.
Hands-on lab debugging skills using JTAG/GDB, logic-analyzers, and oscilloscopes.
Familiarity with Git and build toolchains such as CMake.
BS or MS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent, and 2+ years of professional experience in embedded software engineering.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing bare-metal firmware and working with RTOS environments (e.g., Zephyr, FreeRTOS).
Experience with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test setups, test automation, or firmware CI pipelines.
Knowledge of Embedded Linux and device driver development.
Experience working with optical transceivers, photonic platforms, or high-precision analog/mixed-signal hardware.
Domain understanding in laser physics or wavelength and thermal control systems.
